page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2gne.4xlarge is an x86_64 storage-oriented instance within the Local SSDs family, running on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile comprises a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs using hyperthreading, backed by 33 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 4.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage is provided locally through a 1919 GB SSD, while networking throughput operates at a baseline speed of 5 Gbps. No discrete accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-threaded throughput contrasted with modest single-thread capacity. The instance scored 11753.77 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 12919.13 in PassMark CPU tests, reflecting middle-tier parallel execution capability. Conversely, single-thread performance registered in the lower quartiles, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 18.95 GB/sec. Memory operations show large-block uncached read speeds of 72.03 GB/sec and write speeds of 51.45 GB/sec. In application-level tests, the server delivered 11.71 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and static web serving throughput of 7.66 GB/sec.

The primary resource tradeoff centers on pairing moderate compute clock speeds with integrated high-capacity local SSD storage. Qualitative cost efficiency is highest when software designs take full advantage of the local 1919 GB storage array rather than relying on attached network storage volumes. Due to its throughput limits on single-thread pipelines, it is less suited for latency-critical single-threaded execution or medium-to-large LLM inference. The instance provides an effective platform for local databases, intermediate caching layers, Redis clusters, search index nodes, and distributed data processing pipelines.

Benchmark evaluations show solid multi-core execution, achieving 11753.77 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 11.71 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, though single-core compute speeds and memory latency fall into lower percentiles. The dense local SSD capacity combined with balanced memory-to-vCPU sizing provides qualitative cost efficiency for IOPS-reliant workloads. It is functionally targeted at distributed database nodes, caching clusters, and search index operations that rely on direct local storage throughput.
